source-5d46b41b1dfbd036b889dd17.passage: ICT listing identifies CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024, EN 301 549:2021 IDT, as published May 2024. No V4.1.1 national revision schedule found in the displayed listing. Other work includes accessible AI, authoring tools and cybersecurity; individual projects are outside this narrow verification.

source-cc8183a341f154dba6005b84.passage: SOR/2025-255 registered 2025-12-05, published 2025-12-17 under Accessible Canada Act. Amending s6 inserts ICT standard definition in s19.1 as Canadian CAN/ASC-EN 301 549 as amended. New s19.9(a) permits ETSI editions published more recently than current Canadian ICT standard; (b) also allows immediately preceding Canadian edition within three years of current edition publication. Section18 phases commencement at second/third registration anniversaries. Entity scope and exceptions differ: public entities; private employee thresholds; public-facing transport/broadcast/telecom exclusions and other qualifications. RIAS describes ambulatory incorporation, not completed Canadian adoption of future ETSI revisions.
source-cc8183a341f154dba6005b84.method: web reader, amending sections6-18 and RIAS

source-c064d85912c15e77e6c9f06b.passage: Summary confirms new/updated federal public web pages from 2027-12-05, covered large/medium private web pages from 2028-12-05; mobile/document requirements for public/large private entities from 2028-12-05. Scope differs by requirement and exceptions apply. Page explicitly says summary is not legal text.

source-62f0abcc3f37e094952af536.passage: Who must comply / How to comply: designated public-sector organisations and businesses/nonprofits with 50+ employees; controlled public websites and web content after 2012-01-01. WCAG 2.0 AA except 1.2.4 and 1.2.5; practicability exceptions also described. Page updated 2026-09-21.

source-72ccf29977ef436d80792017.passage: Regulation under Accessibility for Manitobans Act requires WCAG 2.1 AA minimum for newly published web content/content needed to access goods/services and new or significantly updated web applications; exceptions apply.

source-87b837805c7a4f8524b01dd1.passage: M.R.47/2022, English provisions ss2,7,8: phased sector application; relevant web content and new/significantly updated web applications must meet/exceed WCAG2.1AA; feasibility, technology, hardship, control and product-information exceptions. Current version includes 2023 amendment. Bilingual page, English provisions used.

claims.text: Canada’s Accessibility Commissioner reported inspections of federally regulated organisations during 2025–2026 under the Accessible Canada Act and its regulations. The inspections concerned accessibility plans, feedback process descriptions and progress reports. Findings included documents published in inaccessible formats. These findings concern Canadian law. They are not EAA enforcement findings or results from the new ICT requirements due to take effect in 2027.
